---
name: codex-cua
description: Drive local macOS apps from the shell through Codex Computer Use (screenshots, accessibility trees, click, type, key, scroll, drag). Use when a task needs GUI automation on this Mac without SSH, a remote provider, or the cua-ssh app-server setup. For remote Macs or recordings use cua-ssh; for pixel-only VNC targets use cua-vnc.
---

# codex-cua

`bin/codex-cua` exposes the ten Computer Use tools that ship inside Codex as ordinary shell commands, against apps on this Mac. Upstream is [manaflow-ai/codex-cua](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/codex-cua); change `bin/codex-cua` there first, then copy it here.

```bash
./bin/codex-cua doctor
./bin/codex-cua apps
./bin/codex-cua state Calculator --out /tmp/calc.png
./bin/codex-cua click Calculator -m 'Nine'
```

```bash
./scripts/install.sh          # symlinks into ~/.local/bin/codex-cua, so any worktree can call it
```

The symlink follows wherever you ran it from, so re-run it from the primary checkout after a worktree that installed it is removed.

## Why it needs codex

The MCP server is `Codex Computer Use.app/Contents/SharedSupport/SkyComputerUseClient.app/.../SkyComputerUseClient mcp`. Spawning it from a shell fails with `Computer Use server error -10000: Sender process is not authenticated`, because the service checks the sender's parent and responsible team id against OpenAI's (`2DC432GLL2`). So this CLI runs the server the way Codex does: `codex app-server` hosts it, and tools are called through `mcpServer/tool/call` on an ephemeral thread. `doctor` checks that chain, including the signature of the `codex` binary it picked.

## Commands

| Command | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| `apps` | `list_apps` |
| `state <app>` | `get_app_state` (tree to stdout, screenshot to `--out`) |
| `screenshot <app> --out F` | `get_app_state`, image only |
| `find <app> <regex>` | `get_app_state` filtered to `index<TAB>line` |
| `click <app> [-e IDX \| -m REGEX \| --x X --y Y]` | `click` |
| `type <app> <text>` | `type_text` |
| `key <app> <key>` | `press_key` (xdotool syntax: `Return`, `super+c`, `KP_0`) |
| `scroll <app> -d up\|down\|left\|right [--pages N]` | `scroll` |
| `drag <app> --from X,Y --to X,Y` | `drag` |
| `set-value <app> <value>` | `set_value` |
| `select-text <app> <text>` | `select_text` |
| `action <app> <action>` | `perform_secondary_action` |
| `call <tool> '<json>'` | any tool, raw |

`--json` prints the raw MCP result, `--quiet` drops the tree, `--out` saves returned screenshots.

## Element indices are per snapshot

The index column is only meaningful inside the tree it came from. Calculator numbers the digit buttons differently depending on whether the app is frontmost, so `find` in one command and `click -e` in the next can hit the wrong control. Prefer `-m REGEX`, which takes a fresh tree and resolves the index inside the same call. An ambiguous regex fails and lists the first ten hits rather than guessing; pass `--first` when you really want the first one.

Match against text you can see in the tree, and expect two spellings: an unfocused window renders `23 button Nine`, a focused one renders `23 button Description: 9, ID: Nine`. Matching `Nine` works for both, `button Nine` only for one.

## Session daemon

The first command starts a background `codex app-server` holding one thread (about 20s, plus app launch). It stays up, so later commands take well under a second and the app-use session that Computer Use requires stays warm. Interactions auto-prime with `get_app_state` when the app has not been seen yet in the session.

```bash
codex-cua daemon status
codex-cua daemon restart
codex-cua daemon stop
```

Logs are in `~/.cache/codex-cua/session.log`. Use `--no-daemon` for a throwaway app-server when you want no residue (about 5s per command).

## Tests

```bash
cd skills/cua/codex-cua && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Tree parsing and coordinate parsing are covered there. Everything else needs a real app, so verify it by driving one (`state`, `click -m`, then `find` the value that should have changed).

## Rules

Never drive the user's active cmux window with this. Target a scratch app or an isolated window, exactly as with `cua-ssh`. Screenshots are only written where you point them; save anything a human should look at under the repo's `artifacts/<branch>/` tree, not `/tmp`.

| `find <app> <regex>` | `get_app_state` filtered to `index<TAB>line` |
| `click <app> [-e IDX \| -m REGEX \| --x X --y Y]` | `click` |
| `type <app> <text>` | `type_text` |
| `key <app> <key>` | `press_key` (xdotool syntax: `Return`, `super+c`, `KP_0`) |
| `scroll <app> -d up\|down\|left\|right [--pages N]` | `scroll` |
| `drag <app> --from X,Y --to X,Y` | `drag` |
| `set-value <app> <value>` | `set_value` |
| `select-text <app> <text>` | `select_text` |
| `action <app> <action>` | `perform_secondary_action` |
| `call <tool> '<json>'` | any tool, raw |

`--json` prints the raw MCP result, `--quiet` drops the tree, `--out` saves returned screenshots.

## Element indices are per snapshot

The index column is only meaningful inside the tree it came from. Calculator numbers the digit buttons differently depending on whether the app is frontmost, so `find` in one command and `click -e` in the next can hit the wrong control. Prefer `-m REGEX`, which takes a fresh tree and resolves the index inside the same call. An ambiguous regex fails and lists the first ten hits rather than guessing; pass `--first` when you really want the first one.

Match against text you can see in the tree, and expect two spellings: an unfocused window renders `23 button Nine`, a focused one renders `23 button Description: 9, ID: Nine`. Matching `Nine` works for both, `button Nine` only for one.

## Session daemon

The first command starts a background `codex app-server` holding one thread (about 20s, plus app launch). It stays up, so later commands take well under a second and the app-use session that Computer Use requires stays warm. Interactions auto-prime with `get_app_state` when the app has not been seen yet in the session.

```bash
codex-cua daemon status
codex-cua daemon restart
codex-cua daemon stop
```

Logs are in `~/.cache/codex-cua/session.log`. Use `--no-daemon` for a throwaway app-server when you want no residue (about 5s per command).

## Tests

```bash
cd skills/cua/codex-cua && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Tree parsing and coordinate parsing are covered there. Everything else needs a real app, so verify it by driving one (`state`, `click -m`, then `find` the value that should have changed).

## Rules

Never drive the user's active cmux window with this. Target a scratch app or an isolated window, exactly as with `cua-ssh`. Screenshots are only written where you point them; save anything a human should look at under the repo's `artifacts/<branch>/` tree, not `/tmp`.
